commands.author: masatohoshino

target.title: fix(ui): preserve non-minute cron intervals on edit
target.body:
Closes #110033

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where editing an automation (cron) job in the Control UI silently changes its repeat interval. Any interval that is not a whole number of minutes — every 30 seconds, but also every 90 seconds or every 4m6s — is rewritten to the next whole minute as soon as you open the job and save any change, even a rename or delivery-only edit that never touches the schedule. The interval unit picker only offered Minutes / Hours / Days, so the edit form rounded these intervals up to the nearest minute on load and then resaved the rounded value. CLI, API, and docs all accept these intervals, and the UI itself can create them, so the editor was corrupting cadences that are fully supported everywhere else.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a **Seconds** interval unit and reads the stored interval back into the form using the largest unit that divides it exactly (days → hours → minutes → seconds), rendering any sub-second remainder as exact decimal seconds. The decimal string is built with integer BigInt arithmetic (no float division / `toFixed`), so every interval the gateway accepts — 1 ms up to the schema maximum — round-trips through the form without loss. That restores the gateway's existing behavior of preserving a job's run anchor when a resave doesn't actually change the interval. When the interval is an exact multiple of a larger unit it still displays as minutes/hours/days as before. Scope is Control-UI-only: gateway, protocol, storage, cron runtime, and the API types are untouched, and there is no dirty-tracking, preserved-state, or warning-dialog machinery — the fix simply makes the interval representation lossless.

## User Impact

Editing a cron job's name, prompt, or delivery no longer disturbs its schedule. Sub-minute and fractional-minute cadences (e.g. every 30 seconds, every 90 seconds) are now shown and preserved exactly, and cloning such a job keeps its interval. Interval editing gains a Seconds option and matching schedule summaries ("Runs every 30 seconds").

## Evidence

Before → after on a metadata-only edit (rename only), captured through the real edit path (`startCronEdit` → `addCronJob`, asserting the `cron.update` patch):

| interval | before (rounded on save) | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30s | 60000ms | 30000ms |
| 90s | 120000ms | 90000ms |
| 450ms | 60000ms | 450ms |
| 4m6s | 300000ms | 246000ms |

Tests and checks run:

- **UI cron tests: 112 passing** across `ui/src/lib/cron/index.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/cron/view.test.ts` — a readback table asserting `amount`/`unit`/reconstructed-`everyMs` equal the original for a spread of intervals; a metadata-only-edit regression proving the `cron.update` patch keeps the original `everyMs`; a seconds-edit test (45s → 45000, 0.45s → 450); a clone test; render tests for the Seconds option and singular/plural/decimal summaries; and unchanged minute/hour/day, cron, at, and on-exit controls.
- **Gateway anchor invariant: 3 passing** — the existing `src/cron/service.update-recompute-drops-due-every.test.ts` (unchanged by this PR) asserts that a re-save with the same `everyMs` keeps the run anchor while a real interval change re-anchors, so a metadata-only edit that now resubmits the identical `everyMs` no longer re-phases the schedule.
- **Adversarial round-trip coverage**: a broad set of intervals (1, 45, 450, 999, 1500, 30000, 90000, 246000, 3599000, 86399000, up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`) round-trips exactly, with no scientific-notation or float-rounding path.
- `en.ts`-only i18n change (`ui:i18n:baseline` + `ui:i18n:verify` clean); `oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean; `tsgo` clean for the changed files.


### Real setup proof

Verified end-to-end against a **real Gateway** and the **real Control UI built from this PR's commit `5f9ba241a474da834363c9c26ddea2cb8dd1cd51`**, driven in a **real Chromium browser** (Playwright) — not mocked controllers. Isolated throwaway Gateway (token auth, ephemeral state), Node v24.15.0. Per job: create via CLI (`openclaw cron add --every 30s …`), open it in the Control UI editor, change **only the name** (schedule untouched), Save, fully reload the page, reopen the job, then re-read the Gateway with `cron.list`.

**Every 30 seconds**

| step | Control UI editor | Gateway (`cron.list`) |
|---|---|---|
| after create | — | `everyMs=30000`, `anchorMs == createdAtMs` |
| open editor | amount `30`, unit `Seconds`, summary "Runs every 30 seconds" | — |
| rename only, Save | name → `proof-30s-renamed`, schedule untouched | — |
| full reload + reopen | amount `30`, unit `Seconds`, "Runs every 30 seconds", rename persisted | `everyMs=30000` unchanged; `anchorMs` unchanged (still `== createdAtMs`, **not** re-phased to the edit time ~210 s later); name updated |

**Every 90 seconds** — a non-minute interval (1.5 min), the case previously rounded up to 2 minutes:

| step | Control UI editor | Gateway |
|---|---|---|
| open editor | amount `90`, unit `Seconds`, "Runs every 90 seconds" | `everyMs=90000` |
| rename only, Save, full reload | amount `90`, unit `Seconds`, rename persisted | `everyMs=90000` unchanged, `anchorMs` unchanged |

Before this change the editor read both jobs back as whole minutes (30 s → "1 minute", 90 s → "2 minutes"), so a metadata-only Save rewrote the stored interval and re-anchored the schedule.

**i18n:** on the current HEAD, `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` produces no committable changes and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passes. Per the current `ui/AGENTS.md`, generated locale fallback metadata is produced by the post-merge `control-ui-locale-refresh` workflow and is intentionally not committed in a source PR.
